title: I Used NYT Cooking’s New AI-Powered Recipe Modifier, and It’s Actually Pretty Good

claims.claim: The New York Times is using AI in an iOS-only beta to allow subscribers to modify recipes.

evidence.quote: In an iOS-only beta, the Times is now using AI to allow subscribers to modify recipes.

claims.claim: The article announcing the AI recipe modification feature was published on October 23.

evidence.quote: Below the article announcing the change on October 23, commenters loudly aired their grievances
Below the article announcing the change on October 23, commenters loudly aired their grievances...

claims.claim: Commenting for the AI recipe story was turned off after four days and 172 almost exclusively angry comments.

evidence.quote: After four days and 172 almost exclusively angry comments, commenting for the story was turned off.

claims.claim: NYT executive communications director Jordan Cohen stated that the site and app were visited 514 million times in 2025.

evidence.quote: NYT executive communications director Jordan Cohen said the site and app were visited 514 million times in 2025
The Times doesn't share Cooking's subscriber numbers, but NYT executive communications director Jordan Cohen said the site and app were visited 514 million times in 2025...

claims.claim: The NYT Cooking YouTube channel has over 1.4 million subscribers.

evidence.quote: its YouTube channel has over 1.4 million subscribers.
...its YouTube channel has over 1.4 million subscribers.

claims.claim: Earlier this year, the Times allowed AI to help with a recipe-scaling feature and converting from imperial measurements to metric.

evidence.quote: Earlier this year, the Times allowed AI to help with a recipe-scaling feature (modifying ingredient quantities so "serves 4" turns into "serves 6") and converting from imperial measurements to metric—cups, tablespoons, and Fahrenheit to grams, milliliters, and Celsius.

Earlier this year, the Times allowed AI to help with a recipe-scaling feature (modifying ingredient quantities so 'serves 4' turns into 'serves 6') and converting from imperial measurements to metric—cups, tablespoons, and Fahrenheit to grams, milliliters, and Celsius.

claims.claim: NYT Cooking has 60 editors, writers, video journalists, and other employees.

evidence.quote: When I ask what this means for the jobs of 60 editors, writers, video journalists, and other employees—the team that creates the recipes people use and curates the vibe readers relate to—Velasquez stresses that NYT Cooking has been "hiring more than ever"

claims.claim: Camilla Velasquez stated that NYT Cooking has zero intention of publishing fewer recipes.

evidence.quote: Velasquez stresses that NYT Cooking has been "hiring more than ever" and that it has "zero intention of publishing fewer recipes."

When I ask what this means for the jobs of 60 editors, writers, video journalists, and other employees—the team that creates the recipes people use and curates the vibe readers relate to—Velasquez stresses that NYT Cooking has been 'hiring more than ever' and that it has 'zero intention of publishing fewer recipes.'
